question: In its answer to written question E-002523/20261 (ASW), the Commission states that it ‘takes potential health effects of wind turbines seriously, including in relation to infrasound’. It thus confirms the scientific publications describing significant damage to health caused by infrasound and environmental contaminants from wind turbines.

However, the Commission, which, through the European Green Deal, is responsible for the unchecked scaling of wind energy across Europe, is at the same time trying to deny any responsibility. On the one hand, it states that the WHO has not provided any specific limit values or guidelines in relation to infrasound. It then notes that additional research is needed.
And lastly, the Commission points out that the authorisation of wind energy projects falls within the remit of the Member States. 1.
What is the point of the EU working on health issues if it does not introduce limit values (e.g. for infrasound from wind turbines), but just refers to the WHO?
Why is the Commission pushing ahead with the unchecked scaling of wind energy, even though it itself states that it is taking the damage to health seriously?
Why does the Commission want to deny any responsibility, even though it is behind the hasty and damaging rollout of wind energy across the EU?
